correctness.rationale: Hermitian rank-one idempotents are exactly P(a,z)=[[a,z],[z^q,1+a]] with a^2+a=N(z), because trace=1 and determinant=0 imply idempotence via Cayley–Hamilton; norm surjectivity gives 2+(q-2)(q+1)=q(q-1). S=P+Q has ordinary trace 0 and diagonal s; Q=S+P. Requiring both determinants zero leaves a linear relative-trace equation Tr(z w^q)=s²+s+N(w) and one norm=Artin–Schreier equation. For w=0 only s=0 or 1 works, with all q(q-1) choices. For w≠0 the relative-trace affine line has q z-candidates. The absolute trace of N(z) is either a nonzero affine F2-linear functional (q/2 z and two a each, hence q ordered solutions) or identically 1 (zero solutions), with exceptional condition N(w)∈{s²,(s+1)²}. Each allowed nonscalar target count is (q-2)(q²-1), plus two scalars; square weights give exact energy. Independent complete finite-field pair enumeration for q=2,4,8 gives (|P|,support,energy)=(2,2,8),(12,32,768),(56,380,30464), affirming q=2 boundary. Universal statement is proved by field trace algebra, not finite experiments.
